title: The oasis of Khaybar
hookLine: at the oasis of Khaybar, the flag is promised to a man nobody can guess, and given to Ali
last: EVEN HIS ENEMY TOLD THE TRUTH.

cards: A camp outside the oasis of Khaybar, at night, before its fortresses. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, makes an announcement.

Tomorrow, he says, I will give the flag to a man through whose hands Allah will grant victory, a man who loves Allah and His messenger, and whom Allah and His messenger love. Then he says nothing more.
The report says the people spent the night talking it over, each one wondering: will it be me? Today: the oasis of Khaybar.

teach.b: Sahih al-Bukhari tells the morning after. The companions come early, each hoping to be the one. And the Prophet asks a question no one expected: where is Ali ibn Abi Talib?
They tell him Ali has a problem with his eyes. In other words, he's the one person who seems out of the running. The Prophet sends for him anyway.

When Ali arrives, the Prophet applies his saliva to Ali's eyes and prays for him, and the report says Ali was healed as if he'd never had any pain. Then he hands him the flag. Look at Ali's first words.
Not a celebration. A question: shall I fight them until they are like us? And the Prophet's answer slows him down.
Go steadily, he tells him, until you reach their ground. Call them first, and tell them what is owed to Allah.
Then he adds a line that is quoted to this day: that Allah should guide even one person through you is better for you than red camels.
So the man nobody guessed, with sore eyes that morning, is given the task everyone had hoped for.
And the first thing he's taught about it is patience.
Khaybar is a hard chapter. It was home to Jewish communities, and the sirah tells of the fighting, the fall of the fortresses, and the agreement afterward that let its people keep farming the land.
Today's lesson stays with one moment: a flag passing to someone who didn't look ready.

how: Muslims retell the flag at Khaybar from Sahih al-Bukhari as a story about Ali ibn Abi Talib, and the Prophet's line that guiding one person is better than red camels is quoted in teaching about calling others gently.

games.q: the oasis of Khaybar — tap the pairs.

s: the Prophet named Ali the night before
he only described the man; the next morning he asked: where is Ali?
Ali was unwell when the flag was given
his eyes were sore; the Prophet prayed for him and he was healed.
the Prophet told Ali to rush in and fight at once
he told him to go steadily and call them first.

games.q: you're holding the flag. you ask: shall I fight them until they are like us? what does the Prophet tell you?
o: yes, as fast as you can.
go steadily, and call them first.
wait for the others to go ahead.
games.why: go steadily until you reach them, and call them first: one person guided through you is better than red camels.

practice: Bring to mind one hard thing you've been circling, a conversation, a form, a repair, an apology, and notice the reasons you're not ready: tired, unsure, not the right person. Ali had a reason too.
Picture taking it on anyway, one small step at a steady pace, the way he was told: go steadily; if you pray, you can ask Allah for strength in the task in front of you.

wordCard.voice: Khaybar, the oasis where the Prophet gave the flag to Ali, a man promised to be loved by Allah and His messenger. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Khaybar, the oasis named in the hadith.

carryVoice: Your line: the flag to Ali. The man nobody guessed was the one. Day seven hundred eighty-nine, done.
